chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Qa'im will rise, and there is no covenant, nor promise, nor allegiance upon anyone's neck (i.e., he is free from all prior bonds).
ai.seo_question: What does it mean that the Qa'im has no covenant or allegiance upon his neck?
ai.summary: In al-Nu'mani's *Kitab al-Ghayba*, this hadith highlights the Mahdi's political legitimacy by noting he holds no 'bond' (aqd) or 'oath of allegiance' (bay'a) to previous rulers, distinguishing his divinely ordained authority from the caliphal systems. This absence of prior allegiance underscores his status as a fresh, independent leader whose rule is not contingent on the consent of the people or prior monarchs, but is a direct manifestation of God's will.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (4) Muhammad bin Ya’qoob narrated from Muhammad bin Yahya from Ahmad bin Muhammad from al-Husayn bin Sa’eed from ibn Abu Omayr from Hisham bin Salim that Abu Abdullah as-Sadiq (as) had said: “
Al-Qa’im will rise and he has never paid any homage to anyone nor has he had a covenant or a bond with anyone.”
